title: How to remove background in Canva on Mac: step by step, with a transparent PNG export
metaTitle: How to Remove Background in Canva on Mac: Step by Step
description: Learn how to remove background in Canva on Mac, step by step. Covers the Canva Pro requirement, transparent PNG export and fixes for rough edges.
targetKeyword: how to remove background in canva on mac
intro: To remove a background in Canva on Mac, open your design, select the photo, and choose Background Remover from the image tools. Then download the result as a PNG with Transparent background turned on, which the guides I checked say needs a Canva Pro plan.
tldr: Select the photo, open the image tools, then choose Background Remover.
Clean up hair, fur and edges with the Erase and Restore brushes, zoomed in.
Download as PNG with Transparent background turned on. A JPEG keeps the old background.
The guides I checked list the tool as a Canva Pro feature. Check your plan before you start.
The Mac labels in this guide come from browser guides, so compare names on your screen.

blocks.text: What you need before you start

You need a Mac that runs macOS 13.0 or later. That is the minimum the Canva app lists on the Mac App Store. Check your version first. Click the Apple menu, then choose About This Mac. The macOS version appears at the top of the window.

You also need a Canva account and a photo with a clear subject. A person, a product or a pet against a plain wall works well. A busy street or a photo full of reflections is harder for any cutout tool.

items: A Mac running macOS 13.0 or later
The Canva app from the Mac App Store, or Canva in your browser
A Canva account, with the plan checked for the Background Remover
One photo with a clear subject and even light

blocks.text: Which Canva app to use on your Mac

Canva gives you two places to work. One is the Canva app from the Mac App Store, listed as Canva AI Photo & Video Editor. The other is Canva in a browser such as Safari or Chrome. The guides I checked describe the browser editor, not the Mac app.

I could not confirm whether the Mac app shows the same Background Remover in the same place as the browser editor. Treat the steps on this page as the browser flow. Compare each label with what you see on your screen.
Remove the background, step by step

The numbered steps below walk through the full edit, from the blank page to the saved file. Each one comes from a browser-based guide. Menu names can differ slightly in the Mac app, so match the closest name you can find.
Why the Background Remover needs Canva Pro

Two guides, Designkit and Pixelbin, call the background remover a Canva Pro feature. Designkit also says a transparent download needs Canva Pro. Pixelbin lists Canva Pro, Teams, Education and Nonprofits as plans that include the tool.

One search result, from HitPaw, says the tool is free for every user. That conflicts with the other guides. I did not open that page, so I would not plan a project around it. Check Canva's pricing page before you rely on either answer.
If you are on a free account, check whether the tool opens before you rely on it. The guides I checked do not give a clear free allowance, so I have not guessed at one.
Check the cutout before you download
The automatic cutout is only a starting point. Zoom in before you save anything. Look at hair, fur, fingers and the edge of a plastic bag. Those spots tend to keep leftover background.

Designkit suggests the restore or erase tools for hair and fur. Pixelbin suggests the Erase and Restore brushes for rough edges. Work in small strokes, and zoom in again after each pass. Big strokes remove detail you wanted to keep.

Save a transparent PNG, not a JPEG
Transparency only works in PNG files. A JPEG has no transparent layer. Pixelbin says that a file saved as JPEG brings the background back.

In the browser guides, the download path is Share, then Download, then PNG. Turn on Transparent background before you press Download. Skipping that one option can leave the old background in the file.
After the download, check the edges of the subject in your design. Place the PNG on a colored shape. If a white or colored edge shows, download the file again with the option on.
A worked example: a mug on a kitchen table

Say you photographed a white mug on a wooden table, near a window. The mug has a clean handle edge, and the table is busy with grain. That mix is fine for an automatic cutout, but the shadow under the mug is the risk.

Upload the photo, select it, and run the Background Remover. Then zoom in on the shadow. If the shadow stays on the mug base, erase it in small strokes. Keep the handle edge intact, and check it at the same zoom level.
Once the mug looks clean, download as PNG with Transparent background on. Place the file on a colored shape in your design. If the edge still shows a halo, go back and clean it up.
Pick a photo that cuts out cleanly
Good input makes the cutout easier. Use a photo with a clear gap between the subject and the background. A plain wall, a clear sky or a solid color gives the tool an edge to follow.
Light matters too. Designkit says shadows can be read as part of the subject. Shoot under soft, even light, so the shadow stays soft and does not look like a solid shape.
Pixelbin says blurry results come from soft photos. Start with a sharper original. Scaling up a soft photo does not add detail, so keep the original file as your source.
What to check on your Mac version

The Canva app on the Mac App Store listed version 4.234.0 when I checked it. The version before it was 4.233.0. The store page does not describe a background removal change in that update. It covers foldable iPhone support and a larger video timeline.

To check your version, open the App Store, then the Updates tab. If the Canva app is older than 4.234.0, update it. If a menu name still does not match this guide, an update is the first thing to try.
Where Lazur helps when a menu moves
Canva changes its menus. A guide written last year can name a button that has moved. That is where a second pair of eyes helps. Hold ⌥ ⌘, Option and Command together, then ask about your screen.

Ask where the Background Remover is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask for a walkthrough, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click. It does not click for you.
Common mistakes people make

items: Saving as JPEG, which drops the transparent layer
Skipping the zoom check, so a halo reaches the final file
Using a soft, dark or busy photo, then blaming the tool
Assuming the Background Remover is free because a search result says so
Editing the only copy of the photo instead of a duplicate

blocks.text: Keep the original photo safe

Duplicate the design before you remove the background. If the cutout fails, you still have the original layout and photo. The steps are in [how to duplicate a design in Canva on Mac](/how-to/duplicate-a-design-in-canva).
What to do next with a transparent image

A transparent PNG is useful on its own. Place it on a colored background, add it to a flyer, or set it over a photo of a room. Once it is in your design, you can move and resize it like any other image.

If you change the page size, read [how to resize a design in Canva on Mac](/how-to/resize-a-design-in-canva). If you need to line the subject up with text, read [how to align elements in Canva on Mac](/how-to/align-elements-in-canva).

faq.question: Is the Background Remover free in Canva on Mac?
faq.answer: Designkit and Pixelbin both list the Background Remover as a Canva Pro feature. HitPaw, a search result I did not open, says it is free. Check Canva's pricing page before you start a project.

faq.question: Why does my transparent background turn white or show a color?
faq.answer: Pixelbin says the background reappears when the file is saved as JPEG. JPEG has no transparent layer. Download the design again as PNG with Transparent background turned on.

faq.question: Do the Mac app and the browser editor have the same steps?
faq.answer: The guides I checked describe the browser editor. I could not confirm that the Mac app shows the same labels in the same places. Compare each name on your screen before you follow a step.

faq.question: Which macOS version do I need for the Canva app?
faq.answer: The Canva app on the Mac App Store requires macOS 13.0 or later. Click the Apple menu, choose About This Mac, and compare the version number with that minimum.

faq.question: Does Lazur remove the background for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at buttons, draws a circle around them, and guides you one click at a time. It does not click for you. You make the edit, and Lazur helps you find each step.

faq.question: Why does hair look rough after the cutout?
faq.answer: Fine detail such as hair and fur is hard for an automatic cutout. Designkit suggests the restore or erase tools for that. Zoom in, work in small strokes, and check again at the same zoom.

faq.question: What kind of photo works best with the Background Remover?
faq.answer: A photo with a clear gap between the subject and the background works best. Designkit also recommends soft, even light, because shadows can be read as part of the subject.

steps.name: Open your design in the Canva app
steps.text: Open the Canva app on your Mac, then open the design you want to edit. You can also start a new design and bring the photo into it.
steps.tip: The App Store lists the Mac app as Canva AI Photo & Video Editor.

steps.name: Upload the photo
steps.text: In the left panel, open Uploads, then choose the option to upload files. Pick the photo from Finder.
steps.tip: If the photo is already in your Uploads tab, skip this step.

steps.name: Place the photo on the page
steps.text: Click the photo in the Uploads panel to add it to your page. Drag it to the spot you want before you start the edit.

steps.name: Select the image
steps.text: Click the photo on the page so it shows a selection border. The image tools appear once the photo is selected.
steps.tip: If nothing appears, click the photo again. Make sure you did not select the page background.

steps.name: Open the image editing tools
steps.text: Look for the Edit image button, or Edit photo, depending on your version. Designkit's guide uses these names for the browser editor.
steps.tip: If you cannot find the button, ask Lazur to point at it. See the Lazur section above.

steps.name: Choose Background Remover
steps.text: Find Background Remover in the image tools and select it. Designkit's guide files it under a menu with a different name, so match the label you see on your screen.

steps.name: Wait for the cutout
steps.text: Give the tool a few seconds to finish. Pixelbin's guide describes a short wait before the result appears. Do not click again while it works.
steps.tip: If the result looks wrong, you can still clean it up in the next step.

steps.name: Clean up the edges
steps.text: Zoom in on hair, fur and the outline. Use the Erase brush to remove leftover background. Use the Restore brush to bring back detail that was cut away. Work in small strokes.
steps.tip: If a stroke removes too much, undo it right away and zoom in again.

steps.name: Apply the change
steps.text: When the edges look clean, click Apply. Pixelbin's guide includes this step before the download.
steps.tip: Zoom out once and look at the whole subject before you apply.

steps.name: Open the Share menu
steps.text: Click Share, then choose Download from the options.

steps.name: Choose PNG with a transparent background
steps.text: In the download options, choose PNG. Turn on Transparent background, then click Download. Both Designkit and Pixelbin give this path.
steps.tip: If the background comes back later, the file was probably saved as JPEG.

steps.name: Check the file edges
steps.text: Place the downloaded PNG on a colored shape in your design. Check that the old background is gone, especially along the edges of the subject.
steps.tip: If a white or colored edge still shows, download the file again as PNG.

troubleshooting.fix: The file was probably saved as JPEG, which does not support transparency. Download again as PNG with Transparent background turned on.

troubleshooting.problem: Rough edges around hair or fur
troubleshooting.fix: Zoom in, then use the Erase and Restore brushes in small strokes. Designkit suggests the restore or erase tools for hair and fur.
Start from a sharper photo. Pixelbin says blurry results come from soft originals, and scaling up a soft photo does not add detail.

troubleshooting.problem: The Background Remover does not appear
troubleshooting.fix: Check your plan on Canva's pricing page. The guides I checked list the tool as a Canva Pro feature.

troubleshooting.problem: A shadow stays attached to the subject
troubleshooting.fix: Designkit says shadows can be read as part of the subject. Reshoot under soft, even light, then run the tool again.

troubleshooting.problem: Menu names differ from this guide
troubleshooting.fix: The Mac app labels may differ from the browser steps. Update the app from the App Store, or ask Lazur to point at the control.
